newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Eight Moslem refugee houses bombed near Brcko--UN.
newsitem.headline: Eight Moslem refugee houses bombed near Brcko--UN.

text.p: Bomb attacks have badly damaged eight houses belonging to Moslem refugees in the disputed Brcko region of northern Bosnia, a U.N. spokesman said on Sunday.
The homes were in two suburbs of Brcko, a Serb-held town in the strategic narrow corridor that links Serb territory in the west and east.
"Eight strong explosions were heard on Saturday at 2300 in the Brcko area," Andrea Angelli, spokesman of the U.N. police and NATO-led peacekeeping force (IFOR) in Tuzla told Reuters.
According to U.N. police, no one was injured in the attacks, although Agnelli said NATO planned to step up efforts to improve security in the area,
The issue of who should control Brcko was so sensitive that the architects of last year's Dayton peace accord chose to leave the question to international arbitration.
The arbitrators are due to rule on on the town's status by the end of December but Bosnia's former warring factions remain deeply divided on the issue.

Serb authorities have been accused of trying to discourage Moslems returning to homes in the area, in the wake of a series of explosions similar to Saturday night's that have destroyed vacant Moslem houses or those under reconstruction.
Angelli said the U.N. police and IFOR consider the latest bombings to be "a very serious incident.
"They are meeting to try and find a solution to provide security in this area," he said.
